title: Culture Cartography: Mapping the Landscape of Cultural Knowledge
findings: The paper finds that Large Language Models (LLMs) have significant knowledge gaps regarding nuanced, local religious practices, which are a subset of long-tail cultural knowledge. For instance, an LLM might incorrectly generalize Christian traditions (like Christmas) to a predominantly Muslim population (in Indonesia). The proposed 'CULTURE CARTOGRAPHY' method, a mixed-initiative approach involving human guidance, is more effective at identifying these specific religious and cultural knowledge gaps than standard single-initiative methods. Fine-tuning models on data collected with this method improves their performance on related cultural benchmarks.
